known.title: Security: Quote the checkout name in the remote shell command
Data loss: Do not treat an unverified process identity as finished
Data loss: Refuse turn-off when the remote work cannot be inspected
Security: Install the pre-commit check in the hook path Git uses
Functional: Ignore application PID files inside run worktrees
Functional: Report SSH failures throughout setup
Functional: Turn-off fails on hosts with translated process errors

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A developer finishes a round and turns off a Linux machine whose shell uses a French locale. The retained PID names a process that has ended, but only `ps` runs with `LC_ALL=C`; `kill` can emit a translated error, so the English-only match fails and Forge reports that the round still runs. Both turn-off commands then refuse. Error descriptions can depend on the locale, as the [Linux strerror documentation](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/strerror.3.html) describes.
findings.title: Functional: Turn-off fails on hosts with translated process errors

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 5
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - An active round's PID file cannot be opened after Forge has inspected an earlier, finished round. The failed redirection leaves `id` and `start` holding the earlier round's values, and the script ignores the read error. Forge can therefore classify the active round as finished and delete its folder with `--yes`.
findings.title: Data loss: Do not treat an unverified process identity as finished

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A worker runs a Python server with a PID file beside its script, such as `server.pid` beside `server.py` in the worktree. The recursive search still treats that file as a Forge round because the matching `.py` exists. Its PID-only contents lack a start time, so preview and confirmed turn-off both refuse after the Forge round ends.
findings.title: Functional: Ignore application PID files inside run worktrees

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A confirmed turn-off has ignored files and a stash to list before deletion. The new `--yes` assertion checks the loose file and commit count, but not the ignored `notes.txt` or stash that the preview asserts. The test would pass if confirmed turn-off omitted either from its deletion list.
findings.title: Gate: test_5_rounds_on_a_machine_are_off_until_turned_on_and_off_deletes_forges_folder
